chunks: Sahl, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Safwan al-Jammal, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

A man from the hypocrites died, so Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) went out walking and encountered a slave of his. He said to him, 'Where are you going?' He said, 'I am fleeing from the funeral of this hypocrite so that I do not pray over him.' Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) said to him, 'Stand by my side, and whatever you hear me say, say the like of it.'

He said: So he raised his hands and said, 'O Allah! Humble Your servant among Your servants and Your people. O Allah! Cause the heat of Your Fire to reach him. O Allah! Make him taste the intensity of Your punishment, for he used to befriend Your enemies, be inimical to Your friends, and hate the People of the Household of Your Prophet (peace be upon him and his family).'
ai.seo_question: How did Imam Al-Husayn demonstrate the prayer over a hypocrite?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* illustrates the Shia doctrine of *al-Du'a bi al-Naqima* (supplicating for punishment) for the *Nasibi* (those hostile to the Ahl al-Bayt), distinguishing their funeral prayer from that of the righteous. Imam Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) explicitly linked the deceased's spiritual status to his enmity with the Prophet's household, a key criterion in Shia jurisprudence for determining the nature of the funeral supplication. This incident serves as a foundational precedent for the practice of praying for the disgrace of enemies of the Imams rather than seeking their forgiveness.
